title: Why sangha
hookLine: the whole of the holy life is good friendship (SN 45.2)
tomorrow: how did one rich man find the Buddha in the dark?

lines: A FRIEND WHO TEXTS AT SIX.
A SECOND VOICE IN THE CANON.
cards: Some people only make it to the gym because a friend texts at six: you up? Others swear they do their best work alone, headphones in. Mai is the second kind.
After Thursday's sit, the people there asked her to stay for tea and a reading circle, and she'd rather get back to the studio.
She knows the sutta she read with Ava: Ananda calls good friendship half the holy life, and the Buddha says no, it's the whole. But the same canon keeps a second voice. And it sounds a lot like Mai.

teach.b: An old poem in the Sutta Nipata keeps coming back to one refrain: wander alone, like the rhinoceros. Its case is strong. Company brings attachment, quarrels, other people's moods.
Alone, nobody pulls you off course, and nobody's opinion becomes your path. Now the other voice.
Good friendship, the Buddha tells Ananda, is the whole of the holy life, because someone with good friends can be expected to walk the path.
The Pali word is kalyanamitta, a good, lovely friend, and he names himself as one: it's by having him as a good friend that beings are freed. Both are scripture. So which is it?
Listen closer, because the poem doesn't disagree as much as it seems.

teach.h: UNLESS YOU FIND A WISE COMPANION.
teach.b: In the middle of it, it says: if you find a wise companion, someone steady who lives well, walk with them, glad and mindful. Only if you find no such friend, go alone. So the real question is which company.

teach.h: SANGHA, ONE OF THE THREE REFUGES.
teach.b: That's why Buddhists name the sangha, the community, as one of the three refuges, beside the Buddha and the teaching.
Not any crowd. The friends who help you keep walking.

how: Buddhists take refuge in the Buddha, the Dhamma and the Sangha, often reciting the three refuges together at a temple or group sit; monks and nuns live in community, and lay Buddhists meet in temple groups and sitting groups.

o: why monks must live in groups of a set size
why community is called the whole of the holy life
why a temple asks its members to pay dues

games.q: two voices on company — tap the pairs.
p: said friendship is half the holy life
wander alone, unless a wise friend appears

s: the Buddhist ideal is always to practice completely alone
the Buddha called good friendship the whole of the holy life; even the rhinoceros poem says walk with a wise friend if you find one.
the poem that says wander alone also says to walk with a wise companion
if you find a steady, wise friend, walk with them, glad and mindful; only if not, go alone.

games.q: Mai says she practices best alone; her friend says you can't grow without a group. give the rhinoceros poem's best case, in a sentence.
o: company brings attachment and quarrels; alone, nobody's moods pull you off the path.
alone you go faster, and speed is what matters most on the path.
the Buddha wanted his monks to live alone and never in groups.
games.why: that's the poem's real case: company brings ties and moods. and the same poem adds: if you find a wise companion, walk with them.

practice: Think of one person who makes a good habit of yours easier to keep: the one who shows up, who asks how it's going. Write them a short message telling them so.
Send it now or later, your choice, and sit with their face in mind while the sit runs.

wordCard.voice: Why sangha: because good friends, the Buddha told Ananda, aren't half of the holy life. They're all of it.

orig.note: Pali: a good, lovely friend; a friend on the path.

carryVoice: Your line: the whole of it. Alone if you must, with a wise friend if you can. Fourteen days into the block.

sources.ref: Samyutta Nikaya 45.2 (Upaddha Sutta: half the holy life)
Sutta Nipata 1.3 (Khaggavisana Sutta, the rhinoceros), the verses on a wise companion
